# PATHWAYS v1: methods (DRAFT; generated by tools/pathways_methods.py, do not edit by hand)

Five levers on new residential construction in New Zealand, 2026-2050, applied to the baseline projection (baseline-pb-v3.1, reference replacement scenario S3-10) and assessed against the climate-change boundaries of the planetary-boundary layer (acquired rights, AR; ability to pay, AtP). The model is unchanged: `pathways.py` re-calls `engine.forward()` with copies of the reference inputs modified by `levers.py` (hooks: outputs/pathways/HOOKS.md). With every lever off the run reproduces the reference run (maximum relative difference 4.4e-16 over annual carbon, upfront, in-window replacements & repaints, floor area by typology, demand bands, committed range and cumulative LoE; tests/test_pathways.py).

## Conventions

* Years: 2026 is observed (consented floor area fixed) and no lever changes it. A lever at full strength moves a quantity from its baseline value b to its target x as b + w(y) (x - b), with w(y) = clip((y - 2026) / (2035 - 2026), 0, 1): 1/9 in 2027, full from 2035. Sensitivity (P3): full by 2045.
* Near-term market excess (the observed 2026 building above the requirement, fading at rho): frozen at the baseline path, in dwellings, in every run except where L2 absorbs the surplus. It is the observed 2026 pipeline, not demand, so a lever on demand does not change it.
* Bundles: P1 Avoid = L1 + L2 + L3; P2 Shift + Improve = L4 + L5; P3 = all five; each at Moderate (M) and Ambitious (A). Scenarios S1 (Low) and S2 (High) bound P0 and P3 (full Boss runs with `REPLACEMENT_SCENARIO` changed; the levers act on each run's own inputs).
* Accounting as the baseline (time-resolved): within-window carbon = upfront (A1-A5 + soil) in the construction year + replacements & repaints (B2, B4) occurring 2026-2050; later events and all C1-C4 of the 2026-2050 cohorts are committed after 2050 (range: lower with the 2050 factors held, upper at 2025 factors; `events.committed` with each run's floor area by typology).

## Levers as implemented (levers.py)

    L1  size_t(y)       = size_ref_t · (1 − w(y) c_t)
    L2  v(y)            = v0 + w(y) (v* − v0);   join = market_excess(E_nojoin, O26, ρ, 2027, surplus, a)
    L3  demol(y)        = demol · (1 − w(y) d);  resid(y) = resid_LR + (resid_S3(y) − resid_LR)(1 − w(y) d)
    L4  att(y)          = att0 + w(y)(att* − att0); Δ to townhouses / apartments ∝ their held shares; detached −Δ
    L5  A1-A3_t(y)      = [1 − w(y)(1 − r_t)] · (A1-A3_t,2025 − R13_t(y))   (A4-A5, events, C1-C4, soil unchanged)

size_ref: realised new-dwelling size (consented floor area / dwellings, mean of 2023-2025); v0: the 2023 census vacancy held by the baseline; ρ, O26, gap reference: as the baseline near-term rule; resid_LR: the long-run residual (long-run net replacement − BRANZ demolition rate); resid_S3: the S3-10 residual path; R13: the decarbonisation of A1-A3 (Horup et al. 2025, item level). L2 lowers vacancy through the stock identity: while v falls (2027-2035) the vacancy-change term releases existing dwellings once; afterwards only the lower vacancy allowance on new households remains. L4 changes the blended dwelling size and occupancy load factor through the shares (no separate size change). L5 keeps decarbonisation on top of the best-practice ratio.

## Attribution

Shapley value of lever i for the reduction v(∅) − v(N), over all 2^5 = 32 subsets S of the levers N (each subset a full run):

    φ_i = Σ_{S ⊆ N∖{i}} |S|! (5 − |S| − 1)! / 5! · [v(S) − v(S ∪ {i})]

computed in exact rational arithmetic on the run values, so Σ_i φ_i = v(∅) − v(N) = P0 − P3 exactly (tested). v = cumulative within-window carbon (kt) or cumulative LoE AR. The waterfall (pw_1) adds the levers in the fixed order L1 → L5 (Avoid → Shift → Improve); its steps are order-dependent.

## AESA gap

Boundaries B_AR(t), B_AtP(t) for S3-10 from outputs/pb_annual.csv (no lever changes population; every scenario shares the population path). Cumulative LoE = Σ I(t) / Σ B(t) over 2026-2050 (aesa.cumulative_loe); remaining reduction needed = 1 − 1/LoE.

**Back-cast.** I(t; k) = F(t) + k · G(t), where F is the 2026 cohort (its upfront and its in-window replacements & repaints) and G the 2027-2050 cohorts (upfront and in-window events); scaling the floor area of every 2027-2050 cohort by k scales G (the typology mix and the replacement share, hence the soil share, are unchanged). k solves Σ I(t; k) = Σ B_AR(t) (scipy.optimize.brentq on [0, 1], xtol 1e-15; checked against the closed form). For AtP the minimum attainable cumulative LoE is Σ F / Σ B_AtP (k = 0).

**Solution space** (after Horup et al. 2025, Fig. 6): I(t; d, i) = F(t) + (1 − d)[(1 − i) G_ns(t) + G_soil(t)] on P0, with d the uniform cut of 2027-2050 floor area and i the uniform cut of non-soil carbon per m² of the 2027-2050 cohorts (soil and 2026 not cut by i). Bundles are placed at d = 1 − GFA_P / GFA_0 and i = 1 − (C_P / GFA_P) / (C_0 / GFA_0) (2027-2050 cohorts, C non-soil within the window); because the levers also change the soil-bearing share, the grid value at a marker differs slightly from the run (both in backcast.json).

## Checks (tests/test_pathways.py)

* P0 = reference run (≤ 1e-9 relative): annual carbon, upfront, in-window B, floor area by typology, demand bands (boss_results.json), committed range, cumulative LoE AR / AtP (pb_results.json); S1 and S2 P0 = the PB scenario runs.
* Each lever at zero strength = the baseline; 2026 identical in every run; lever functions never modify their inputs.
* Shapley efficiency exact; D ≥ S × OLF in every year of every run (engine `extra_clip` = 0); implied vacancy ≥ 4.0%; no negative dwellings built; back-cast LoE AR = 1 (≤ 1e-9).
* Baseline outputs byte-identical to tag baseline-PB_v3.1 outside outputs/pathways/.

## Limitations

* L3 lifetime extension is an upper bound: the carbon of renovating the buildings kept in use is not modelled (Napiontek et al. 2025, Resour. Conserv. Recycl. 215, 108117).
* L1 Ambitious is weaker than Moderate: the 1991-1995 realised sizes of townhouses (124.2 m²) and apartments (110.9 m²) exceed the 2023-2025 sizes, so both are held and only detached dwellings are cut (4.74%).
* L5 Ambitious rests on a single case study per typology (detached SD_2, A1-A3 88.3 kg/m² against the pooled 166.7); apartments are held (one independent case study). The ratio is applied to the pooled A1-A3 of every item, so the best-practice material mix is assumed transferable to the whole typology.
* L2: v0 = 5.39% is the published 2023 empty-dwelling share while the target range (4.01-5.38%) is on a consistent definition (pooled 2018/2023 empty share of unoccupied); the targets are rounded to 0.1 point. Vacancy reduction acts once, through the stock identity, while the rate falls.
* L4 changes the typology shares only: dwelling size and occupancy load factor per typology, and the per-typology carbon and soil factors, stay as in the baseline.
* The near-term excess is frozen in dwellings, so its floor area follows L1 and L4 through the blended size.
* Each lever is a parameter change on the baseline model; no behavioural, market or rebound response is modelled; interactions between levers are those of the model (attributed by Shapley values).
* The pathways are deterministic (median demographics); the Monte Carlo and the boundary sensitivities of the baseline are not re-run for them. Boundaries are static (PB layer limitations apply).
* Omitted in v1: Occupancy / household size (household size is a demographic input of the baseline (Stats NZ household projections, Boss.HH_SIZE_VARIANT) and sets the number of households, not a construction choice; a lever on it needs a behavioural or policy model of household formation that v1 does not have); Brownfield soil (the soil factor is one area-weighted value for Auckland land zoned for urbanisation (Christoforatos, Pickering & Schipper 2026) and soil is already zero on the replacement bands; no national brownfield share is in the inputs to parameterise a shift); Lightweighting (the case studies give A1-A3 per m2 by material and item, not structural mass by design alternative; a mass reduction cannot be separated from the material choice already covered by L5); Bio-based archetypes (no typology has a bio-based archetype among the 16 case studies, and the model's biogenic-carbon convention (timber C1-C4 excludes biogenic CO2) would need extending; overlaps L5).
